set.body:
MEASURED 2026-08-30 from package storymodel4s.probes, outside align:

  StructuralMemberEstimate    mirror=true  fromProduct=true  copy=false  apply=false
  StructuralMemberExclusion   mirror=true  fromProduct=true  copy=false  apply=false
  StructuralReduction         mirror=true  fromProduct=true  copy=false  apply=false
  StructuralReductionReceipt  mirror=true  fromProduct=true  copy=false  apply=false

All four are declared `private[align]` (align/cost.scala:195, :205, :231, :218). THAT CLOSES THE TWO DOORS PEOPLE LOOK AT AND LEAVES THE TWO THEY DO NOT. A Mirror.ProductOf derives from any package and fromProduct takes a bare tuple, so every one of them is constructible from anywhere in one line.

WHY THIS ONE IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY FORGE. StructuralReductionReceipt IS AN AUDIT RECEIPT -- its own scaladoc says 'Audit receipt for a segment-level structural reduction', and its fields ARE the attestation: which reducer ran, which members were estimated, which excluded, and the coverage over both the source chart and the observed estimates. A forgeable audit receipt can attest a reduction THAT NEVER RAN, with whatever coverage its author prefers.

StructuralReduction then pairs an Estimate[Double] with a StructuralReductionReceipt, so the forge mints the FALSE TUPLE directly: an estimate from one computation carrying the receipt of another. That is precisely what the private constructor was added to prevent.

CONTEXT THAT MAKES IT SHARPER: this is the STRUCTURAL CHANNEL, the one embed-grakern feeds -- and today we established that the Semantic channel was never semantic. A receipt that can attest an unrun reduction sits badly beside that.

PROBE LANDED FIRST, pinning the known-bad state: align/src/test/scala/storymodel4s/probes/StructuralChannelUnforgeableSuite.scala. Its assertions currently assert the doors ARE open. WHEN THIS BEAD IS FIXED THOSE COURTS GO RED and the repairer must flip each assert deliberately -- a silent repair and a silent regression must not look alike.

FIX SHAPE, not decided: the sweep-1 remedy was making the type a plain final class with a private constructor and an explicit accessor set, which defeats Mirror derivation. Whoever takes this should confirm that remedy still holds in Scala 3.7.4 with a positive control before applying it to four types.

Found by the chief while finishing bd-01M183VBPNEAPT5JNQMBMYMKQ9 (sweep 3), whose remaining population was 5 types, 4 of them these.
set.title: align: the four structural-channel types are forgeable through Mirror and fromProduct -- including an AUDIT RECEIPT
